questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Prove that two distinct nonvertical lines with the same slope m are parallel.
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that two distinct nonvertical lines with the same slope m are parallel.
questions.correct_answer: mx + b₁ = mx + b₂ gives b₁ = b₂, a contradiction; so the lines never meet and are parallel.
questions.required_method: Write the lines as y = mx + b₁ and y = mx + b₂ with b₁ ≠ b₂ and show there is no intersection.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: equations with equal slopes and different intercepts; solving for an intersection leads to b₁ = b₂ (false); conclusion. Alternative: a translation maps one line to the other; or congruent slope triangles with corresponding angles equal.

questions.prompt: Line OA passes through O(0, 0) and A(a, b) with a, b ≠ 0. Rotating A 90° counterclockwise about O gives A'(-b, a). Use this to prove that perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is -1. The diagram shows the case A(3, 2).
questions.prompt_markup: Line OA passes through O(0, 0) and A(a, b) with a, b ≠ 0. Rotating A 90° counterclockwise about O gives A'(-b, a). Use this to prove that perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is -1. The diagram shows the case A(3, 2).
questions.correct_answer: slope OA = b/a, slope OA' = a/(-b) = -a/b, product -1.
questions.required_method: Find the slopes of OA and OA', then their product.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: a 90° rotation maps OA onto a perpendicular line; the image of (a, b) is (-b, a); slopes b/a and -a/b; product -1. Any pair of perpendicular nonvertical lines can be translated to pass through O, keeping slopes. Invalid: checking only the one example.

questions.prompt: Prove that two distinct nonvertical lines that are parallel have equal slopes.
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that two distinct nonvertical lines that are parallel have equal slopes.
questions.correct_answer: If m₁ ≠ m₂, then m₁x + b₁ = m₂x + b₂ has the solution x = (b₂ - b₁)/(m₁ - m₂), so the lines meet, contradicting parallel. So m₁ = m₂.
questions.required_method: Indirect: assume the slopes m₁ and m₂ are different and find an intersection point.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: assumption of unequal slopes; solving for the intersection; contradiction with "parallel"; conclusion.

questions.prompt: Prove that if two nonvertical lines have slopes m and -1/m (m ≠ 0), they are perpendicular. (Translate both lines so they pass through the origin first.)
questions.prompt_markup: Prove that if two nonvertical lines have slopes m and -1/m (m ≠ 0), they are perpendicular. (Translate both lines so they pass through the origin first.)
questions.correct_answer: (1, m) rotates to (-m, 1), on the line with slope 1/(-m) = -1/m; so the line with slope -1/m through O is the 90° image of y = mx, hence perpendicular.
questions.required_method: Rotate the point (1, m) on y = mx by 90° about the origin and find the slope of its image line.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: translations keep slopes; the rotation image of (1, m); its slope -1/m; a 90° rotation image is perpendicular; only one line through O has slope -1/m.

questions.prompt: Rhombus OABC has O(0, 0), A(a, 0), B(a + b, c), C(b, c), with b² + c² = a². Prove that its diagonals are perpendicular.
questions.prompt_markup: Rhombus OABC has O(0, 0), A(a, 0), B(a + b, c), C(b, c), with b² + c² = a². Prove that its diagonals are perpendicular.
